feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 2 (10 cm span, 12 cm track, y 0.04 m) cut oval line losses to 0.05 per run, but slalom stayed at 1.0 and s-bend at 0.9, with max_error about 0.061 to 0.064 m. Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.10 m) removed oval losses but cut oval progress from 0.51 to 0.14 and left slalom at 1.0 loss per run. That makes the drivetrain the wrong lever for the tight-bend losses, and this candidate tests sensing timing instead. If slalom and s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1.0 per run with max_error below 0.06 m and oscillation at or below 0.3, keep the forward sensors and move on to gains for progress. If losses stay near 0.9 to 1.0 with max_error still about 0.06 m and oscillation at or below 0.3, the tape is still leaving the sensor span on tight bends, so widen the outer sensors. If oscillation rises above 0.3 (iteration 2 oscillation was 0.23 to 0.27 on oval and s-bend), the forward offset is overshooting, so reduce footprint lag rather than moving the sensors further.
requested_changes: If slalom and s-bend line losses stay at about 0.9 to 1.0 per run with max_error still at or above 0.06 m and steering_oscillation at or below 0.3, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 m (sensor_size 0.012 kept), since the 6 to 8 cm and 10 cm spans in iterations 0 to 2 showed span changes only moved oval losses.

If steering_oscillation rises above 0.3 with losses persisting (iteration 2 gave 0.23 to 0.27 at y 0.04 m), set sensor_size to 0.016 m at y 0.06 m, because the 0.12 m track change in iteration 3 did not reduce slalom losses, so turn response is not the limit.
Keep wheel_track at 0.12 m. Iteration 3 at 0.10 m cut oval progress from 0.51 to 0.14, so do not narrow the track again unless slalom losses fall and progress holds.
